newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arab League hails new Intifada, slams Israel.
newsitem.headline: Arab League hails new Intifada, slams Israel.

text.p: An Arab League meeting on Thursday praised the Palestinian demonstrations against an Israeli tunnel near an Islamic holy site and urged the Jewish state to stop making changes in the disputed city.

Forty Palestinians and 11 Israelis have been killed in two days of clashes in the self-rule areas as Israeli troops and Palestinian police exchanged gunfire and Palestinians hurled stones at Israeli soldiers.

The Palestinian Authority told the emergency meeting that Israel had declared war on Palestinians after clashes broke out in Palestinian self-rule areas in the West Bank and Gaza Strip following the opening of the tunnel in Jerusalem.

"The Council of the League hails the intifada of the Palestinian people, with the participation of its leaders, in intrepidly confronting Israeli repressive practices," the league said in a statement after the meeting.

"The Council...considers what is happening to be part of an Israeli Zionist plot to destroy the Aqsa mosque, set up the Temple of Solomon, obliterate Islamic Arab landmarks and create more facts which harm the legal status of Jerusalem," it added.
The meeting, at the level of permanent delegates, said Arabs still wanted peace.

"The Council calls on Israel to immediately halt all hostile measures before it is too late and to prevent the region from returning to the vicious circle of violence, instability and bloodshed," it added.

The Palestinian delegate to the Arab League, Mohamed Sobeih, told a news conference at the end of the meeting: "Netanyahu and the Israeli government speak about peace while practicing a state of war. The situation is very dangerous".
He predicted a cycle of violence if hardline Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu did not fulfil promises made in peace talks between Israel and the Arabs.
"Not one Palestinian or Arab will accept a peace that is at the expense of Palestinian and Arab land or rights," Sobeih said.
"Otherwise Netanyahu will not succeed and will drag Israel into a whirlpool of violence and extremism. This Israeli terrorism will reflect badly all over the world," he added.
The Arab League statement urged the world community to intervene quickly to "force Israel to stop all measures and practices aimed at obliterating (Islamic) holy places".

"The peace process is in more danger than you can imagine because of Israel's action, which is completely unacceptable," Arab League Secretary General Esmat Abdel-Meguid said. "We place responsibility for this on Israel."
Sobeih urged Arab states at the start of the meeting to isolate and "punish" Israel in retaliation for its conduct.

The Palestinian delegate said it was time for Arab states to carry out the threat they made at the June Arab summit to reconsider deals with Israel if Netanyahu refused to abide by peace deals signed by his predecessor. Netanyahu came to power on a platform opposed to giving back Arab land.
"The time has come to put into effect the resolutions of the last Arab summit, to prove to Israel and the world that we are worthy to defend our national rights," Sobeih said.
"The Palestinian people will continue to defend Jerusalem and our legitimate national rights, with everything they possess and whatever sacrifices it costs."
